briefings.title: Gemini 4 Argon: What’s new and what’s next
briefings.tldr: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Argon, an advanced AI model featuring an industry-leading one million output tokens, refined writing quality, and deep integration into internal engineering workflows by 100,000 Googlers prior to launch.

briefings.title: Google's AI Infrastructure Chief, Amin Vahdat, on the Physics & Economics of Frontier AI

people.name: Amin Vahdat
people.role: Chief Technologist for AI Infrastructure, Google

briefings.tldr: Amin Vahdat, Google's AI Infrastructure Chief, discusses the massive capex buildout, arguing that "goodput" (useful work delivered under real failure conditions) matters more than theoretical FLOPS, while detailing co-design strategies, power bottlenecks, optical networking, and future architectures.

briefings.title: Eric Schmidt, ex-CEO Google : 25 ans dans la Silicon Valley
briefings.channel: Matthieu Stefani - Génération Do It Yourself
briefings.tldr: Former Google CEO and technologist Eric Schmidt discusses geopolitics, modern warfare in Ukraine, the exponential acceleration of artificial intelligence, and management strategies for the modern CEO.

briefings.title: “Russia and Ukraine are inventing the future of war”: former Google CEO Eric Schmidt | The Economist
briefings.tldr: Eric Schmidt warns that Russia has accelerated its wartime innovation to match Ukraine’s, combining advanced jet shahads, glide bombs, and upcoming satellite networks into a strategy of "total war" that requires urgent Western funding and scale to counter.

briefings.title: Why AI Should Be Regulated, and Embraced: Google’s James Manyika | The Mishal Husain Show

people.name: James Manyika
people.role: SVP of Technology and Society, Google

briefings.tldr: Google’s James Manyika argues that the AI industry must simultaneously race to unlock transformative societal opportunities—such as scientific discovery and crisis prediction—and rigorously manage safety risks.

briefings.title: The Future of War and Global Power: Can the West Innovate Fast Enough?

people.name: Dan Driscoll
people.role: Former United States Secretary of the Army

briefings.tldr: Eric Schmidt and Dan Driscoll discuss how software-driven warfare and rapid AI integration are transforming global conflict in Ukraine, arguing that Western defense ecosystems must urgently modernize their data infrastructure, adopt open architecture, and scale hardware production to outpace adversaries.

briefings.title: Jeff Dean: The 1% Rule for Building in AI
briefings.tldr: Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean and YC’s Diana Hu discuss AI progress, hardware breakthroughs, inference scaling, and why small teams can win by focusing on context engineering and niche problem domains.

briefings.title: Sameer Samat on Android 17 and the Future of Intelligent Computing
briefings.tldr: Google is transitioning Android from a traditional operating system into an "intelligence system" driven by user intent rather than manual inputs.

briefings.title: 2026 GCEPS Reunions Talk: The AI Revolution with Eric Schmidt
briefings.tldr: The AI revolution is advancing at an exponential pace, shifting from next-token prediction to emergent reasoning capable of solving highly complex, un-trained scientific problems.

briefings.title: Yossi Matias on the golden age of research

people.name: Yossi Matias
people.role: VP & Head of Google Research, Google

briefings.tldr: Google Research is driving a new "golden age of research" by accelerating the "magic cycle" of innovation—an iterative loop that rapidly translates breakthrough scientific discoveries in climate, medicine, and quantum computing into scalable, real-world tools that amplify human capability.

briefings.title: What Happens After A 1,000,000x AI Compute Leap? | Jeff Dean
briefings.tldr: Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean asserts that physical limits on AI training data, model precision, and context windows can be bypassed through synthetic data generation, extreme hardware-software co-design, and cascading retrieval systems.

briefings.title: Gemini co-leads on project origins and what's next
briefings.tldr: The Gemini project was established by consolidating Google's fragmented AI research teams and compute resources into a unified effort.

briefings.title: How Sundar Pichai is rethinking Google for the AI era | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Following Google I/O, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai details how he restructured the company to build a unified AI infrastructure, while addressing critical challenges surrounding the impact of AI agents on the open web, energy grids, and the future of Search.

briefings.title: Sundar Pichai Opening Remarks | I/O 2026 Keynote
briefings.tldr: Google has entered the "agentic era" of AI, driven by a massive infrastructure scaling up to $190 billion in capital expenditure and model usage processing 3.2 quadrillion tokens monthly.

briefings.title: Sundar Pichai on Whether Google Is Falling Behind in A.I.
briefings.tldr: Google CEO Sundar Pichai acknowledges that while Google remains a frontier leader in multimodal AI, it currently lags behind competitors in agentic coding, but he remains highly confident that Gemini 1.5 Pro scaling, systematic search evolutions, and robust hardware infrastructure will secure Google's long-term leadership.

briefings.title: Beyond the keynote with Sundar Pichai
briefings.tldr: At Google I/O 2026, Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the industry's shift toward agentic workflows and the critical need for cost-efficient "workhorse" models like Gemini 3.5 Flash.

briefings.title: Building the quantum-AI future with Hartmut Neven and James Manyika

people.name: James Manyika
people.role: SVP of Research, Technology, and Society, Google

briefings.tldr: Google’s Quantum AI division is rapidly accelerating its timeline toward commercial viability, demonstrating breakthroughs in below-threshold error correction and quantum machine learning that lower the hardware threshold for practical applications and mandate a transition to post-quantum encryption by 2029.

briefings.title: Developer Keynote (Google I/O '26)
briefings.tldr: At Google I/O 2026, Google announced a massive shift from assistive AI to autonomous agents, driven by Google Antigravity—a unified agentic development platform designed to build, deploy, and orchestrate AI agents seamlessly across Cloud, Android, and the Web.

briefings.title: Innovation, Investment, and Partnerships: Eric Schmidt at Milken 2026
briefings.tldr: The United States must pivot from antiquated, high-cost military platforms to autonomous, AI-driven robotic systems to maintain global deterrence while addressing a $40 trillion national debt that now costs more in interest than the entire defense budget.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis Wants to Build AGI. Should We Trust Him?
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning founder of DeepMind, is driven by a unique blend of scientific rigor and "spiritual" ambition to build AGI, balancing a high-stakes rivalry with OpenAI against his desire to remain a "good" steward of humanity's most powerful invention.

briefings.title: Eric Schmidt: Singularity's Arrival, 92-Gigawatt Problem & Recursive Self-Improvement Timeline | 241
briefings.tldr: The world is approaching a "superintelligence moment" within two to three years driven by recursive self-improvement and AI agents, but this progression faces a critical 92-gigawatt power shortage and intense competition from China’s vertically integrated robotics industry.

briefings.title: AI Summit 2026 LIVE: Google CEO Sundar Pichai Speaks at India AI Summit | N18L
briefings.tldr: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced a "full-stack commitment" to India’s AI future, centered on a $15 billion infrastructure investment, the goal of skilling 10 million people, and the deployment of localized AI products for healthcare, agriculture, and search.

briefings.title: LIVE: Google CEO Sundar Pichai speaks at India AI Summit | Global South | Artificial Intelligence
briefings.tldr: Google is investing $15 billion in Indian infrastructure, headlined by a new "full-stack AI hub" in Visakhapatnam, as part of a broader "bold and responsible" strategy to ensure AI drives scientific breakthroughs and economic inclusion without creating a new digital divide.

briefings.title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai Envisions 'Extraordinary' AI Boom for India, Unveils US Connectivity Drive
briefings.tldr: Google is deepening its "full-stack" commitment to India through major infrastructure investments—including new subsea cable routes—and strategic partnerships with the Indian government to digitize the civil service and empower 11 million students with GenAI.

briefings.title: PM Narendra Modi Holds Meeting with Google CEO Sundar Pichai | India AI Impact Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Google CEO Sundar Pichai at the India AI Impact Summit 2026 to discuss the future of artificial intelligence and solidify India’s position as a global leader in technological innovation.

briefings.title: Former Google CEO On The Importance Of Human Expertise In An Increasingly Automated World
briefings.tldr: Artificial intelligence, initially explored by Google, is now a pervasive and rapidly accelerating force fundamentally reshaping global economies, workforce demands, and societal structures, necessitating strategic investment in agentic AI, astute leadership to navigate ethical challenges, and concerted efforts to educate the public on its transformative benefits.
